8
The acceleration of free fall on Pluto is 0.66 m s–2.
An object weighs 6.0 N on Earth.
What would this object weigh on Pluto?
A
0.40 N
B
0.93 N
C
4.0 N
D
39 N

hints: Notice the object has a weight of $6.0 \text{ N}$ on Earth but its mass in $\text{kg}$ stays the same on Pluto.
Recall weight is $W = mg$, so first use Earth $g \approx 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ to find the mass from $6.0 \text{ N}$.
Multiply that same mass by Pluto $g = 0.66 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ to get the new weight, which must be much smaller than $6.0 \text{ N}$.
walkthrough: Identify what is the same: mass $m$ does not change when moving from Earth to Pluto, but weight $W = mg$ changes because $g$ changes.
Find the mass from Earth data using $m = W/g$. Take Earth $g \approx 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Apply $W = mg$ on Pluto with $g = 0.66 \text{ m s}^{-2}$: $W_{Pluto} = 0.612 \times 0.66$.
Calculate: $W_{Pluto} \approx 0.40 \text{ N}$ with unit $\text{N}$, much less than on Earth as expected for small $g$. This is option A.

B.explanation: A weight of $0.93 \text{ N}$ is too large for $g = 0.66 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ and does not follow $W = mg$ with the mass from Earth.

C.explanation: Treating $6.0 \text{ N}$ as $6.0 \text{ kg}$ gives $6.0 \times 0.66 \approx 4.0 \text{ N}$, which forgets to find mass from Earth weight first.

D.explanation: Multiplying instead of dividing by Earth $g$, $6.0 \times 9.81 \times 0.66 \approx 39 \text{ N}$, reverses $m = W/g$.
